about.title: About Calorie Calculator
about.description: The Calorie Calculator estimates daily calorie needs based on age, gender, weight, height, and activity level. It calculates Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) and Total Daily Energy Expenditure (TDEE) so you can review maintenance, weight-loss, or weight-gain scenarios. Use the results as formula-based estimates and adjust based on real-world response and guidance from qualified health professionals when needed.

faq.q: What's the difference between BMR and TDEE in calorie calculation?
faq.a: BMR (Basal Metabolic Rate) is the calories your body burns at rest for basic functions like breathing and circulation. TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) includes BMR plus calories burned through daily activities and exercise. The calculator shows both values as planning estimates.

faq.q: How should I interpret calorie calculator estimates?
faq.a: Calorie calculators provide formula-based estimates using population averages. Individual metabolism can vary, so use the result as a starting point and adjust based on your actual progress, energy levels, and guidance from qualified professionals when needed.

faq.q: How should I use the calculated daily calories?
faq.a: Use the calorie result as a baseline. Monitor your weight, energy levels, and progress, then adjust intake as needed based on your response and broader goals. The calculator provides a formula-based starting point.

faq.q: How often should I recalculate my daily calorie needs?
faq.a: Recalculate your calorie needs every 10-15 pounds of weight change, or every 2-3 months if your activity level changes significantly. Rechecking the inputs helps keep the estimate aligned with your current situation.

faq.q: What activity level should I choose in the calorie calculator?
faq.a: Be honest about your activity level: Sedentary (desk job, no exercise), Lightly Active (light exercise 1-3 days/week), Moderately Active (moderate exercise 3-5 days/week), Very Active (hard exercise 6-7 days/week), or Extremely Active (very hard exercise, physical job).

faq.q: Can I use this calorie calculator for weight loss?
faq.a: It can be used as a starting point for weight-loss planning by estimating maintenance calories and showing lower-intake scenarios. Because individual response varies, review changes gradually and consult healthcare providers when you need individualized guidance.
